name: Crawler Record
author: dizzysoft

sections.description:
Crawler Record logs the last time specific user agents (Google, Bing, OpenAI, Anthropic, Perplexity, DuckDuckGo, plus your own) accessed your content:

  • Per-post meta box: “Crawler Record” shows each crawler’s last visit and robots status for THAT post’s path.
  • Admin page: a grouped list of all crawlers, with last seen time, last page, and robots status for the configured home path.
  • Admin Bar (front-end): quick-glance status for the current singular or URL context (no dropdowns in wp-admin).

Robots-aware, no network fetch: The plugin renders robots.txt locally (physical file or WordPress virtual output via do_robots) and evaluates Allow/Disallow rules for a given path. If Settings → Reading → “Discourage search engines” is enabled (blog_public = 0), all agents are shown as blocked with a prominent warning.

Performance-friendly by design: Write-throttling (default 10 minutes, filterable) and an auxiliary “last post ID per agent” record avoids heavy admin queries on large sites.

Privacy-friendly: Saves only bot visit timestamps and last URLs crawled — no personal data.

Highlights

  • Supports common user-agent variants for Google, Bing, OpenAI (GPTBot / OAI-SearchBot / ChatGPT-User), Anthropic (ClaudeBot / Claude-User / Claude-SearchBot), Perplexity, DuckDuckGo, plus customizable entries.
  • Robots status computed from local robots.txt (physical or virtual) without outbound requests.
  • Clear UI with grouped sections, microsecond timestamps, and a small diagnostics toggle showing the matched robots group and rule.

Known limitations

  • robots.txt wildcards (*) and end-of-line marker ($) are not interpreted; matching is prefix-based only. Future versions may add full spec support.

Privacy

This plugin stores:
– Timestamps of crawler visits (float, with microseconds)
– Last URL seen per crawler (per-URL records)
– Last post ID per crawler (for admin performance)

It does not collect or store personal data about site visitors. No data is transmitted to third parties.

License

GPLv2 or later. See LICENSE file.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install via the admin Plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Visit Crawler Record under Admin → Crawler Record to review crawler activity.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin block bots or change robots.txt?

No. It only observes visits and evaluates your current robots.txt settings. It doesn’t block, rate-limit, or edit robots.txt.

Why do I see “Blocked by WordPress setting”?

If Settings → Reading → Discourage search engines is enabled, the plugin marks all agents as blocked and shows a red notice.

How does the plugin read robots.txt without a network fetch?

It first checks for a physical robots.txt in your site root. If not present, it invokes the same WordPress hook path that renders the virtual robots.txt (do_robots), so SEO plugins are reflected.

How often are timestamps written?

By default, at most once every 10 minutes per agent per resource. Filter dzcr_throttle_window (seconds) to adjust.

short_description: Track when selected web crawlers (Googlebot, Bingbot, GPTBot, Claude, Perplexity, DuckDuckGo, etc.) last viewed your site’s pages.
